utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation heard on English channel] We're making a lot of decisions this morning and that's why we are starting a few minutes late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please. I am receiving interpretation in English on number four. I'm not receiving interpretation in --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The interpreters are requested to switch channels, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English interpretation, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now we heard you speak in English. It is on channel 4 -- at least mine is on channel 4. Well, I'm going to say something else and I'm not receiving any interpretation, so basically that means that it should be solved. We'll see. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow on a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good morning to you, and you may sit down. Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney, lead counsel for the Prosecution, together with co-counsels, Ms. Patricia Sellers and Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for the Accused Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Vasvija Vidovic together with Mr. John Jones I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. I wish to inform my learned friends that Mr. Geoff Roberts will be authorised to correspond with them as well as with representatives of Chambers and registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I thank my learned friend for this confirmation. We consider that we can use this contact with Mr. Geoff Roberts to address the whole Defence team in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Before we bring in the witness, after we closed last Friday, I wasn't really expecting this but my attention was drawn to the fact that I did not give instructions to the Prosecution in particular, and for that matter to the accused that no communications were to take place between Prosecution and -- not the accused, - sorry- the witness, and between the witness and others in relation to his testimony. My impression and my brief and also of my two colleagues is that this is a rule which is applied without any exception here in this Tribunal and that everyone is aware of it, but once the matter has arisen we are going to pronounce ourselves on it to make things clear, abundantly clear, for the purpose of this trial at least. The Trial Chamber as composed, that's myself, Judge Brydensholt, and Judge Eser, we are seeking to clarify the position of the Trial Chamber regarding the issue of communications between the parties and the witnesses. The Trial Chamber notes that this oral ruling in no way indicates that any of the parties has acted improperly, but rather views this order as a reminder to the parties of a well-established practice applied by this Tribunal across the various Trial Chambers, and respective of the legal tradition the various Judges come from. We note that indeed there is nothing in the Statute or in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal which expressly addresses this subject, but again that would have been almost something that would -- one would not really expect in the statute for sure and in the regulations also, because it's a matter of principle that is applied universally. We note, however, that a witness either for the Prosecution or for the Defence, once he or she has taken the solemn declaration pursuant to Rule 90(A) of our rules, that witness becomes a witness of truth before this Tribunal and is no longer merely a witness for either of the two parties, depending on who has produced him or her. We further note that Rule 90(F) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, according to which the Trial Chamber shall exercise control over the mode and order of interrogating witnesses and presenting evidence so as to make the interrogation and presentation effective for the ascertainment of the truth has a bearing on this matter in that it imposes on the Trial Chamber a measure of control. The Trial Chamber considers that allowing either party to communicate with a witness after that witness has commenced giving evidence orally may lead to both parties -- to both party and -- both party producing that witness and witness discussing the contents of his or her testimony in a way that is not consonant with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the Statute of this Tribunal. Since it may, albeit, and we consider sometimes innocently and unwittingly, influence the witness's further testimony. The Trial Chamber therefore orders that once a witness either for the Prosecution or for the Defence has made the solemn declaration pursuant to Rule 90(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal and commenced giving evidence -- giving oral evidence, neither the Prosecution nor the Defence can or may communicate with that witness on the subject of the contents of his or her testimony, except with the special leave of the Trial Chamber. We further order that in the event that a witness wishes to contact the party that called him or her, he or she must first inform the competent staff of the Victims and Witnesses Section, which in turn shall refer the matter to the Trial Chamber. In addition, the Trial Chamber notes that the obligation bore by a witness to refrain from discussing the contents of his or her ongoing testimony also extends to the public and lasts until his or her testimony comes to an end. We finally request that a copy of this oral decision will be communicated to the Victims and Witnesses Unit, Mr. Registrar, with specific instructions, with specific instructions, to that unit to make all witnesses aware of this duty and responsibility that they have. Thank you. Having disposed of this, are there any preliminary matters that you would like to raise before we bring in the witness and proceed with his testimony. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday evening there was contact by the Defence team towards our team informing us and updating us of the time needed for -- by cross-examination of the witness of today. Defence counsel may correct me if I'm wrong, but the message was that Defence need the whole trial day for this cross-examination. And if that's right that has also ramifications for the Victims and Witnesses Unit. So we updated the Victims and Witnesses Unit with a view to scheduling of the witnesses, and we are really regretting the fact that at such a late time Defence counsel raised this issue of consuming or planning to consume the whole day rather than a couple of hours as projected. And I appreciate that on further studying it might be needed for, but it is rather late. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately -- yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's not that we were late in informing the Prosecution, but when you asked me last time whether I would be able to finish the cross-examination today I said yes, yes I will be able to complete the cross-examination today. I will of course do my best to be as expeditious as possible, but I do have quite a number of questions and quite a number of documents to show to the witness. And in view of the fact that the Prosecution also extended their time and put forward new facts not previously mentioned in the witness statements. So bearing in mind that the Prosecution took more time than was planned, I will have to clarify the points that were raised. I will of course try to do this as speedily and as expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. But let me say one thing and then we will discuss this, Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser. There may come a time, which can be pretty soon, that if we notice that you are deviating from the plans that we have made as far as allocation of time for the hearing of the various witnesses, we may step in and stick to the time that was indicated and say: You have to finish your examination-in-chief in one hour; you have to finish your cross-examination in one hour. We may have to do that if you disappoint us, in other words if you go beyond the time that you yourselves have indicated, then we will step in, then we will step in. So any further preliminary matters? I see none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal once more. I hope you had a good rest these last few days and that you are fresh enough to resume your testimony. May I remind you that you are testifying under solemn declaration, which we all heard you make last Friday. Before you start giving evidence I want to make sure that you are receiving interpretation of what I am telling you in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And I have one question before you start giving evidence. Over the weekend, since you finished giving evidence last Friday, did you speak with anyone, did you talk with anyone, about your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Mrs. Monica and Mrs. Marija told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mrs. Monica, these are from the victims, I suppose. Yeah. What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They told me I shouldn't meet with any other witnesses or with any lawyers and that I should not talk about my testimony because I am under oath, and I abided by what they said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So then I thank you, and that's exactly what you should have done and I appreciate that you are confirming that that's precisely what you did. So let's proceed, yes. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I continue my cross-examination, I simply wish to check whether the last exhibit, or rather the last piece of evidence I wish to tender, page 43 of the book: "The Bloody Christmas of the Village of Kravica" by Boro Miljanovic, whether this has been given an exhibit number. That was the end of the first part of my cross-examination. I wish to tender this into evidence and ask that it be given a number if it hasn't already got one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, it has already been -- it is being numbered as D12. It is being numbered as D12.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Simic. I will try to make your testimony easier today. We will continue where we left off. Mr. Simic, last Friday you told us a few things about Mr. Miladin Bogdanovic. You told us a few things about Mr. Miladin Bogdanovic. You said that he was the person who organised the first meeting of your villages in order to set up a village guard. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later you said that he gave you a piece of paper calling you to join the village defence.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 12th of March, 1992, that's when it started.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Simic. Miladin Bogdanovic then in other words organised you and the other men from the village of Jezestica to form a village defence?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he was quite authoritative when carrying out the organisation of the village defence?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he was or not, but he talked to us and he said whoever had a house should also join the village guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you this, Mr. Simic, is that you said at one point he even threatened that the village guards would set fire to your house if you left the village defence when you wished to do so.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that he was a violent man?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was violent or not, but that's what he told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said in your testimony and also in answer to my question on Friday that the defence line of the village was organised around the hamlets of the village of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said to be sure that you didn't know who organised the defence line, whether the SDS or somebody else. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I didn't know. Had I known, I would have told Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miladin Bogdanovic was a member of the SDS, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not aware of that at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please put on the ELMO document number 00835837, which is an excerpt from the list of members of the SDS of Bratunac, and this is a document disclosed to the Defence by the Prosecution. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Can the witness take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can you see the document before you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at number 663 Miladin Kostadin Bogdanovic Jezestica, born in 1934, and the number of his SDS admission, and also he gave a contribution of 100 dinars voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know whether he was a member of the SDS or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the personal details that I have just read out to you, do they correspond to the details of Mr. Miladin Bogdanovic, the one you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did say he was born in 1934?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I move that this list of members of the SDS, page 00835837 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection, if Your Honours please, but with the caveat that the Prosecution doesn't accept necessarily the authenticity of this document, but as to its admissibility and its weight, well, that's another issue. So there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this would be D13, no?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, is it possible that Mr. Bogdanovic organised the defence of the village on behalf of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not clear to me. I never heard about this. All I know is that he said we had to have a village guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know whether he organised this on behalf of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I knew that I would say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO a map of the Kravica area. This is part of a larger map by the Military Geographical Institute for the Zvornik region and the scale is 1:10.000. This is the same map. It was published in 1971. That was used by my colleague Mr. John Jones last Thursday which the Prosecutor has seen, and then I wish to put a few questions to the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Last Friday we talked about certain villages and hamlets and we talked about where the lines were. Bearing in mind the exhibit I showed you last time, Mr. Simic, the line quoted on page 43 of the book: "The Bloody Christmas of Kravica," and bearing in mind the description of that line, I marked in orange the places mentioned in that description. I would now like to ask you to look at the map and the places that I have marked in orange. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you say whether this is Banovici, Banjevici, Gornja Brana, Donja Brana, Bacici, Bratinci [phoen], Dolovi, Djermani, Jezestica, Magasic, Jezero, Mandici, and Bandera?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. Each of these villages had its own village defence around the houses, just as Jezestica did, with its hamlets. The same happened in Kravica and its hamlets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there was a defence in these villages and you can confirm that? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a village defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't know who established these lines. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I don't know that. If I did know, I would tell you. I said on Friday I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, do you know that the Army of Republika Srpska was in command of those lines, in command of the people manning those lines?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that either. I was part of the village guard on the 12th of March, 1992, and I was released in March 1993. I can tell you what I saw and did then. I can't tell you anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, just -- I'm not objecting so much to the question, but what I suspect may be a failure to clarify issues with the witness. If Madam Vidovic is putting to the witness that the Army of Republika Srpska was in control of his village defence and/or other village defences in the area, then of course she should put that, if that's part of her case, to the witness. It's not entirely clear from her question whether or not she is suggesting that, but it seems to be inherent in her question. It's a very simple matter. Just ask the

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: in Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic, I think it's the case of maybe putting your question again in a clearer matter. You asked the question to the witness: "Do you know that the Army of Republika Srpska was on the 12th of March, 1992" -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the one before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the one before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, do you know that the Army of Republika Srpska was in command of those lines, in command of the people manning those lines? As it is, it moves up while I am reading. Could you rephrase the question to reflect actually the point of Mr. Di Fazio, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is only one in a string of questions I will put in this connection, but before this I wanted the map to be given a number and then I will come back to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It will be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D14, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D14. But the thing is, Madam Vidovic, is the map we are seeing on the monitor cannot be exactly said that is the same thing we were given. The one that we were given does not bear any highlights. So I think if you are going to tender this map as an exhibit, you need to have it marked. And in this case I would even suggest that since you are asking this particular witness questions on a marked map, this marked map will only refer to this particular witness so that we don't mix it up with other witnesses. So it will be admitted as D14, but it will be marked and also initialled by the witness so that we will know exactly which map he was being questioned about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just while we're on that topic, if Your Honours please, we'll need to get the same highlights. I'm actually quite happy to do that with the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We can mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can go along now, we can go ahead now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then it will be marked later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're not going to waste time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The witness has confirmed that these are the places that were mentioned and that is why I move that this map be admitted into evidence. I will now continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I will now put the following question to you: Were you aware that the lines in these villages were under the control and command of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, it wasn't. I never heard or saw the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher put on the ELMO a part of the document: "The War History of Bratunac. The circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the beginning of the war," page 00641760, disclosed to us by the Prosecutor along with receipt number 14. I ask that this document be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the part right under number 00641760 which says: In mid-April 1992, a Crisis Staff was formed in Kravica headed by Nedjo Nikolic. The staff determined the defence lines in the area of Kravica, from Banjevici, Donja Brana and Gornja Brana, Bacici, Jezero, Mratinjaci, Gornji Dolovi, Donji Dolovi, Brezanci, Jasikovaca, Ravni Buljim, Jezestica, (Jaglic, Burmani, and Vresinje), Magasic, Mjenice, Radukici, Bozici, and Deronjici, across Avdagina and Mandic to Bandera. The first commander of the Kravica area defence was Lieutenant Colonel Marko Lukic followed by Lieutenant Brano Jovanovic, Lieutenant Zoran Ostojic, and the 2nd Lieutenant Lazar Ostojic. Mr. Simic, this is a description of the same line of defence we have just been talking about running through the same villages and it says that the first commander was lieutenant colonel Marko Lukic. Do you know that this man was the first commander of the defence of the Kravica area, which included your village? Did you hear about this man ever?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him. I never heard of him. I cooperated only with Miladin Bogdanovic, and he was the one who gave us all the information we got.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that Mr. Bogdanovic had any contacts with this man?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I would say so if I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you will agree that this is again a description of the same defence lines that we have just been talking about and that the defence of Jezestica included the hamlets of Jaglici, Djermani, Vresinje and the nearby village of Magasici?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the village of Jezestica and the hamlets of Djermani, Rankovici, Kijevici, these were all linked up to Magasici. I know what the village guards were like in our village. I don't know about other villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I move that the front page and the part of the document I quoted and showed to the witness be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It will be given an exhibit number D15. A proprio I would like to raise this matter: You stated earlier on, Madam Vidovic, that this document was disclosed to you by the Prosecution. Was it just these two or three pages that were disclosed or the entire book? Do we have the front page of the title, the publisher, so that we will have it annexed to this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honour, the Prosecutor has disclosed only one part of this document, therefore of the book which is entitled: "The Circumstances Prevailing in Bosnia-Herzegovina Prior to the War," but it does describe this part of the event, and that was done against the receipt number 14. Your Honour, during these proceedings, I will most certainly try to locate the remaining part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we are interested in is the front page, the title of the book, the publisher, the ISBN number, and the date of publishing, printing, et cetera. Judge Eser would like to put a -- put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I would like to come back to a question we already posed to you last Friday. When you speak of defence lines, do you mean it in terms of a line -- lines around the village only or you are proposing that they are -- had been a defence line between the various villages? So "defence lines" is a vague description. Was it only a surrounding the villages or the line connecting different villages?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are talking about defence lines in this particular case armband around the villages. However the area of Kravica consists of many villages. And during this day and my cross-examination, you will also see that these other villages have their own defence systems as well. And this will come out very clearly through the cross-examination that I intend to pursue today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, isn't it true that when you spoke about the area that you call Brdo or Brda, that you had in mind, Rankovici, Kijevici and Djermani hamlets, or what is also known as Stara Jezestica. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, in these hamlets, too, there were defence lines. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, village lines of defence. That's how we referred to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it true that on the 8th of August, 1992, precisely these village lines of defence were under the attack that was set up in those hamlets?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Jezestica hamlets were attacked on the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will now refer to Defence document D7, and I kindly ask the usher again to put on the ELMO the map that we had just used earlier and which I think had been marked D14. That's the map in fact that we had used earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I also kindly ask you to show to the witness our document D7, that's the list of staff members and the logistics of the Territorial Defence of Kravica, including the TO unit list in the Kravica area. Let me just remind you or ask the witness just to look at the front pages of the list of these members and to see whether it refers to Kravica, Donji Bacici, Mandici, Brezanci, Dolovi, Siljkovici, Lazarici, Marici, Gornji Bacici, Jezero, Ocenovici, Banjevici, Popovici, Mratinci, Jezestica, Magasici, and Kajici. Could you please just look at this and see whether these villages are listed there.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that what you showed me before, and I am not familiar with these names --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are saying you are not familiar with these names?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the map that I showed you a little earlier and see that these places were marked in yellow. For example, Kravica. Could you please put the map on the ELMO. I kindly ask the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. usher to put the map on the ELMO. Mr. Simic, can you see these places better from the map. I will start from the top. There is Ocenovici, Opravdici, Popovici, Bacici, Donja Bacici, Kravica, Marici, Siljkovici, Lazarici, Lipenovici, also Jezestica, Dolovici, Siljkovici. Can you please look at the map and these where these villages are?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I'll put you a simple question with regard to this. Are all these Serbian villages rather populated by the Serbs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct and true that the people from these villages were involved in the defence of this area?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know the names of those men that I saw. I know the men from Jezestica, and the others I only knew by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, last Friday you told us that you had not been involved as a conscript in the Jezestica II Company.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was included near Jezestica on the 20th of March, 1992. It is not correct that I wasn't involved. I was involved is what we called village guards, but I never saw a list according to which I was paid any salary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later, Mr. Simic. What you in fact ascertained was that you were only a member of the village guard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I now kindly ask the usher to put the ELMO -- again the Defence exhibit D7 showing members of the staff of logistics of Jezestica, and I would draw the attention of the witness and the Chamber and the Prosecution to page 01320326. Could the witness please look at this page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can you see it? Yes, we have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Simic, that in this document, for example, for the village Donji Bacici, the village guard was listed completely separately from other conscripts from this village?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. I had no idea whether it was related to the conscripts or whether it was an independent village guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that it's written on the document: Village guard, and there are the names there?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them. Perhaps I knew them by sight from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, please. I'm not objecting, but I'm just not following this evidence. Could Madam Vidovic tell me where it says the word "conscripts" or there's some separation of village guard from conscripts, other conscripts. I've got page 326 and I see -- and I refer back to the English translation, it says Donji Bacici, and then village patrol was crossed out, and then gunners. So I don't see anything about conscripts or -- a lot of the matters that were inherent in the questioning, I'm just trying to follow, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I will explain this in very simple terms. Our document D7 is entitled: "The list of members of the staff and the logistics system of Kravica." And that refers to the Territorial Defence of Kravica. And then on the page that I just mentioned we have a list of the members of the Territorial Defence which are soldiers, and below that we have a village guard as a specific category. And I just saw now that in the English version, and it says: Village patrol. It is correct that it has been crossed out but I was quoting and citing the original of the document. And in the course of the proceedings we shall see why that was the case. Your Honours, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic, because I think we need to make this clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, this document begins with number 01320325 and it refers to the list of the Kravica staff and Territorial Defence followed by a series of units. I drew your attention to the document 01320326, which is an integral part of these seven. And after the list of the members of the staff and units of Donji Bacici, you can see a list of a few names under the heading of: Village guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's also crossed, both in the original and in the English translation. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Because the original document is such and we shall see from other forthcoming documents why that was the case. Of course this is exactly how the original looks like and that is why I am showing it to you. And it is very significant that this list has been crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you said that you didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again. No objection, Your Honour. And I'm just trying to follow -- sorry, which people? Every one in the document? Part of the document? The village guard? I have no problem with this kind of questioning, but I want to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again because it's not clear to us either. Are you referring the witness only to that part which is crossed out, the village guard? That's how I understood it, but I want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely that, Your Honours. And I kindly ask now the witness, and this will further clarify the situation, to look at page 01320334 of the same D7 document, which has the list of Jezestica II. Can you please push the document a little bit upwards so that we can see the end of it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you can see that underneath those names there is no indication that they were village guards. Isn't that true? And I will repeat the page number 01320334. Mr. Simic, is it true that there is no mention of the village guard here?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not written there, but that's how we dubbed it. There was no other name assigned to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Simic. Let me put to you a few more questions in this context. Your father's name is Gojko. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born in Gostilj and you lived in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Last Friday the Prosecution asked you if your father's name was Ljubo and you said no. Now, I will ask the usher to produce on the ELMO the extract from the federal census bureau referring to the municipality of Srebrenica and Bratunac, which contains the list of all the persons whose last name is Simic. In the attachment to this extract is a letter of the director of the statistics bureau who provided official information to the defence council on the names of persons who were listed in the 1992 census in Bratunac municipality, Srebrenica, and Zvornik municipality. The name of Mr. Miladin Simic, father's name Gojko, born in Gostilj residing in Jezestica is on page 4. Mr. Simic, could you please look at this page and see whether this is your name. On the next page, somewhere in the middle, you can see Simic, Gojko, Miladin, Jezestica, Gostilj. This is your name, right?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please have this extract from the statistics bureau referring to all these municipalities and listing all the persons with the last name Simic together with the covering letter to be given an evidence number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be D16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which is D15?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you are the only person, Miladin Simic, who was a resident of Jezestica in 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your name is on the list, too, in document 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You even received remuneration for your participating in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me. Maybe somebody else did but I didn't. I didn't know why that was the case because I also held guard and I received salary from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put on the ELMO document number 133527, list of the VP members, 2465/5 who received payment for business official trips and a document containing the financial document of the Bratunac Brigade. It was taken by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, could you please look at this document. Can you see this document, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2081.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you push the document upwards, please. Yeah. A little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 2081 it says -- or you can see the name: Miladin Simic. And it says from the 1st of August until the 31st of August, 1992, and the amount of 13.020 dinars. Mr. Simic, you did receive this money, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not true. I said that I had received no money even after I had been released.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document 0132335207, the list of the persons who received remuneration for business trips in August 2, 1992, and numbered 2465/5 be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be D17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In addition to that just to complete the question -- the witness's question -- answer, I would like the technicians first to zoom on what appears to be number 281 with the words: "Simic, Miladin" so that he can see it --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2081, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry, 2081. It's further down.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you just push it up a little bit. A little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And is that the best you can -- because I am going to ask you now to move towards the right so that where there are signatures so that the witness sees the signature that appears there. You need to move, you need to move further. Yes. And there is one on the monitor three, four, five, six, seven, eight, the eighth entry, the eighth signature from the top. Could we zoom on that any further, please. Yes. Okay. And perhaps he can tell us whether he recognises that signature as his own.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I ask you now that next to this witness you put on the ELMO the statement given by Mr. Simic and signed by him quite clearly in 2001. If at all possible, could you fold over this part with Mr. Simic's signature. Fold it. Here we can see Mr. Miladin Simic's signature. Would you now, Mr. Usher, please fold this part over. I can give you my copy if you like with Mr. Simic's signature and place it next to the other signature. It's marked in yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you see now, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's similar, but I wouldn't say it was my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Simic, these are financial documents. Why would your name be listed here and your signature appear if you did not receive this amount of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He said that's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's changed it a little bit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He says it looks like his, but it's not his, his position remains the same, and he's being asked: Now, why is his signature on the document. You can draw your own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Objection sustained, in fact. But it does, Madam Vidovic, also draw your attention to the second statement that he released to -- made to the Prosecution, then he decided to sign in block letters. So we -- that can't be of an end. His other statement is signed in block letters. Yes, the Trial Chamber will draw its conclusion if it can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, all the units on your territory were paid by the Army of Republika Srpska, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that before the soldiers were paid or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking of units, Mr. Simic. Are you aware that they were paid by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard there was some kind of village troops receiving payment, but I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO a document which is an excerpt from the payroll of August 1992, which was taken from the financial records of the Bratunac Brigade, and it bears the number 01335185. This excerpts that I wish to show the witness bears the number 01335186 and the title, "list of salaries paid for August 1992". Please put the document on the ELMO and let the witness see it. This is the English version. Could you please put the Bosnian Herzegovinian version. The document is salaries paid for August 1992. Mr. Simic, is it not correct that this document lists the precise amount paid in the Kravica area as salaries. We have a document here for the 22 units mentioned in document D7. Is that not correct, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know anything about this. I don't know how much was paid or who received it. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Simic. Please look at number 9 of this document which mentions the unit Jezestica II and it received 599.480 dinars.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this, but it's not clear to me. I didn't hear about it. I don't know what they received.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What didn't you hear, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about this amount of money and whether they received it or not. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I move that this document which is an excerpt from a larger document starting with 01335185 and the part bearing the number 01335186 bearing the title, "Salary for August 1992" be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be D18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Vidovic, did you obtain this from the Prosecution, this document? I see an ERN number on --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. Yes. These documents we are using are confiscated from the Bratunac Brigade by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simic, I will put another question to you. The Bratunac Brigade was established in November 1992, and that was a big event in the Bratunac region, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you perhaps aware of what happened with these units and as you call them guards as of November 1992 and onwards? Did they become part of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I neither saw nor heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are you trying to say that you were not a soldier of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the village guard from March 1992 to March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now put on the ELMO document number 01319781, which is a list of persons belonging to military post number 2465 through 5 who received remuneration for official travel for November 1992, and this was confiscated from the financial documentation of the Bratunac Brigade and has been previously shown as Defence exhibit D8.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D8.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 88, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I wish to draw your attention now to page 01319786 which has the 3rd Infantry Company. This is 01319786 and it's number 356, Miladin Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you push the document up a little bit, please. And the page ends with the numbers 9788.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please -- I may have misquoted the page number. Would you please turn -- yes, yes. Number 356 is here, Simic, Miladin, and that's number 356. He was there in that company from the 1st of November to the 30th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could you please move this document a little bit to the right -- to the left, sorry. Yes. And he received the amount of 48.900 dinars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you were a member of the Bratunac Brigade after all, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you I did not receive this money. And you can see in my military record when I joined the village guards and when I left the village guards. I don't know who compiled this list, but I know that in March -- I don't know now whether it was the 20th or the 25th of March, that I was released. But who it was who compiled this list you can check in the military records.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are you trying to say that you were in the village guards until March 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this connection I will ask you the following: Do you know that the village guards as of November 1992 was not treated as army at all in the area where the Bratunac Brigade was active?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is that I did not go any further from my house. This was a village guard. When there was an attack on the 7th of January, we went to Colakovici and Popovic. We were evacuated there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer the questions I put to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher put on the ELMO document number 01320311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just copies, if Your Honours please. We -- I don't think we received a copy of the last document that was used with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one? This is D8. The last document is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The last one. Not the one being put now but the document with the salaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this is D8. It has already been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was tendered last Friday or during the testimony of the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we look at this document and allow the witness to reply to my question and then it might be a convenient time moment for a break if it suits Your Honours. Would the usher please put on the ELMO document number 01320311 which is an order from the command of the Bratunac garrison dated the 5th of November, 1992. I ask that the witness look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document is an order ordering all persons keeping guard in the village guards saying that we cannot provide them with wages and the commanders of the basic units should not include such persons in the lists for -- in the payroll?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I will put a question to you to which you may know the answer. As a member of the village guard, you were not able to receive a salary from the Bratunac Brigade nor could you have been put on the list of its soldiers in 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what I think unless something dirty was done. Because in my booklet it says clearly when I was in the village guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I ask that document 01320311, order from the command of the Bratunac garrison of the 5th of November, 1992, be admitted into evidence and I wish to mention once again that this document is part of the confiscated financial documentation of the Bratunac Brigade, confiscated by the Prosecutor. Thank you, Your Honours. This might be a convenient time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And this document will be D19. I recognise Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just one very minor matter. I wonder if the Defence would be so kind to inform the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber which particular seizure are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You're referring -- confiscation from the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said very clearly that these are confiscated documents seized from the Bratunac Brigade. The Office of the Prosecutor disclosed two CDs to us with this, and I think they should know how and when these documents were confiscated. I did not go into it now because I focused on the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think that's fair enough. I was just wondering if the information was at hand. If it's not, we can make our own inquiries. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you can make your own inquiries for sure. I hope so, at least. So, we'll have a break of 25 minutes. I'm saying 25 and not 30 so that we try to economise on time as much as we can so that possibly we finish with the cross-examination today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I -- wait. Okay. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a short question; it relates to the time needed for -- on cross. I already announced that to Defence counsel. But when we take a look at the projected witness subsequent to this one, that particular witness is not brought to the Tribunal this morning upon this information that the cross might be needed for the whole day, otherwise it would -- that witness would wait and wait. My question is: Is it true we will take this morning, the whole morning, and so on for cross, and that means for me that I can confirm that she doesn't need to be stand-by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Wubben. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, hopefully I think that I will need another one and a half hours minimum, and I will really try to be focused and to finish within this time limit. Perhaps ten minutes plus or something, but I really will try to finish by 1.00 p.m.. It of course depends on the course of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.00 p.m., between half 12.00 and 1.00, you know, we have a break. So any way I am not going to tell you what to do, Mr. Wubben. I mean, you've heard what Madam Vidovic had to say and regulate yourselves accordingly. I don't know. We will be here. We are at your disposal until quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If you are at our disposal and if it's true that it can be finalised, cross, around 1.00, 1.15, then it means a start for three-quarters of an hour. And if that's productive, and I would accommodate the Trial Chamber to proceed in an expeditious way, that will mean then -- if that's the case, that will mean that I will request our team to contact Victims and Witnesses Unit to let them stand by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the reverse. It's not you accommodating us; it's we accommodating you, basically. And amongst the things we recognise is we don't know what this witness is going to say, we don't know whether it's suitable for you to start and continue tomorrow. I don't know. It's up to you. But we are not going to -- what we are telling you is: We are at your disposal, and at your disposal of course until quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next thing, Ms. Vidovic, my attention has been drawn during the break to appeal to you to slow down because you are making the life of the interpreters more difficult than it ought to be. All right? Can I count on your cooperation as well as on yours, Mr. Simic? Please allow an interval of time between question and answer because you are not even allowing one another to finish the sentence. This happens when you speak -- both speak the same language.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, let us resume where we stopped. In your statement on Friday you mentioned that there was artillery in the area of your local commune deployed in Siljkovici and Rankovici. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the VRS army was not -- did not exist, or rather that you didn't know anything about that in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anything about it nor did I see. I encountered the local people of Jezestica only.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Simic, then who gave the artillery weapons to the village defence? These were not shotguns. Is that true? Or hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But there was only one in Sipovici and one in Rankovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This kind of weaponry must have been provided by either the Army of Republika Srpska or the JNA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never heard from anyone about this. I knew that there was a small recoilless gun then. I'm not familiar with that weapon, and I never saw it. I never was interested to go over there and look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Is it true that the area of Kravica in fact had much more artillery than you had stated here?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. I never heard of it and I didn't go to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I'm speaking about the Kravica area, I'm a also referring to the surrounding villages of Siljkovici, Rankovici, Jezestica, et cetera. You are a hunter and you know very well what the Kravica area is. I'm not referring to the village of Kravica only, but to the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear to me but I didn't see anything deployed, either in Rankovici, or Siljkovici, but I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be again shown document D7 so that he can again look at page 01320326 which is part of our Defence Exhibit D7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, in this document under the column of the village guard in the village Bacici, there's also a list of artillery operators with 24 names underneath. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this but it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, could you please look at these names. You must know some of them because those were your neighbours. Could you please look at the list.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stojan Milosevic was a teacher of my daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a gunner?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could -- however, since this is already an exhibit, it doesn't need to be assigned a number. But could you please now put on the ELMO our exhibit D6 again, page number 00656784 which refers to Ocenovici and Banjevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, could you please take a look at this. You said you were a hunter and that you were very well familiar with the area. Could you tell us please, was there a hunters' lodge in Banjevici that you know of?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear of it but I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a hunter you never went there?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my region. We had our own regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document now that is in front of you and which refers to Ocenovici and Banjevici. In this document in the last column, there is also a list of gunners and it consists of 16 names. In this regard let me ask you: Gunners are men that serve artillery weapons; that is the definition in our language of the term "gunner." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But I don't know these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you had never heard that there were artillery units in these two villages?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never got familiar with that nor did anyone tell us that there were artillery weapons deployed anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what is happening. We are still receiving interpretation. He started answering your question when you had not even finished it. And you, Madam Vidovic, put -- started putting the same -- the next question when he hadn't finished as yet and when we were still halfway through the interpretation. We can't go on like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether the word "gunner" is used for the people who work with artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But I don't know any of these names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you perhaps hear that heavy artillery was deployed in Vresinje above Radukici which is also in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also never heard about that. I only know that there was a gun in Rankovici and in Siljkovici. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Simic. Where then these artillery weapons at Siljkovici, Rankovici were pointing at or what did they target?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. I don't know where it was aiming at or what were their targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There is something about this evidence and the way it's coming out that's concerning me. The evidence of this witness you recall on Friday was that he had not laid eyes on these two weapons located in Siljkovici and Rankovici. And I don't recall his precise word but he said something to the effect that he knew or somehow knew that this was a weapon that could be carried by you and me. You recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, the way it's coming out in the transcript is we're moving from something he heard about that could be carried by a human being to an artillery weapon. Now, I'm no arms expert but in English the term "artillery" tends to have a connotation of a much larger, much more powerful weapon than something that can be carried by a human being. That's what I'm concerned about. And indeed you can see that Madam Vidovic is assuming that this object, whatever it was, could have been targeted or was used in a certain fashion. So we're going -- we're entrenching into the transcript the concept of some sort of artillery weapon, when in reality this witness has spoken about something he says he didn't actually lay eyes on and that could be carried by a human being. And that perspective must be maintained in the transcript. And that's my only concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think having heard that -- yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may respond. When I'm asking questions I bear in mind whether the witness has any knowledge of that. If he mentioned artillery -- in our language can also refer to either light or heavy artillery, and I think that the witness understands me perfectly well. I would also like to draw your attention to the statement made on the 7th of April, 2002, where he specifically says that there were guns in Siljkovici and Rankovici and that there were deployed -- that artillery guns were deployed there and this is precisely what I'm discussing now with the witness. Now I'm referring to page 3 of the witness's statement given on the 7th of April, 2002, which he for the most part repeated here. And if I may, Your Honours, I would like to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But taking stock of what you mentioned, Mr. Di Fazio, also the fact that he has given evidence on this and also what Madam Vidovic -- so we are -- we'll proceed. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are we talking about the Serbian army in Siljkovici and Rankovici?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes. The guns in Siljkovici and Rankovici, one each there, were Serbian guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were those weapons shooting at the Muslim population or the Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know? Why would they shoot at the Serbian population? I assume that they shot at the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me proceed to another issue, Mr. Simic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just a one very brief transcript matter and it should be clear because it's this very issue that we talked about. Line 20. "Q. Mr. Simic, are we talking about the Serbian army in Siljkovici and Rankovici." I heard the question as: Are we talking about Serbian artillery in Siljkovici and Rankovici. And there's a big difference in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard exactly like you did, Mr. Di Fazio, and I would like Madam Vidovic to correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. You're not wrong. I asked the question about the Serbian artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. And thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, is it true that the women were extensively involved in the combat operations on the side of the Serbian people? I'm not going to refer at this point to the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I heard the women were not involved in the fighting fought by the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the entire platoons of women in the area of Bratunac were involved as part of defence system or defence units?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of that or never saw such a thing. It may have been the case but since I have no knowledge of that, I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the usher please put on the ELMO document number 00656840 which also originates from the seized documentations of the Bratunac Brigade, from Bratunac, and which is entitled: "The list of women that are to be paid salaries for August 1992." Will the witness please look at this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There's a list of 35 women. The person under number 1, it says here that she is a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. What kind of platoon are we talking about? I really don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the women's platoon. Mr. Simic, could you please look at the heading of this document. You know what the heading or the logo of the document is?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Simic and Madam Vidovic, we are back to square one. It is you, Mr. Simic, that is causing all this trouble. Allow an interval of time after Madam Vidovic has put her question to you. What she has just stated needs to be translated to us because we don't understand your language. And therefore, allow an interval of time before you jump in to answer her question. I know that you are showing a lot of enthusiasm and try to do your best and answer your questions -- the questions put to you as precisely and as fully as you can, but we can't make the life of the interpreters and also of the recorder difficult.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't want apologies, I want cooperation, Mr. Simic. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, this is a list of women who are to be paid salaries for the month of August 1992 and the person under number 1, it says, is the platoon commander. Did you hear that women were members of the defence in your area? I am asking you again.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't hear about that. I didn't. I did not hear it. I did not see it. These women did not come round and I can't say that before Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move that this document, the list of women on the payroll for the month of August 1992, number 00656840 be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D20 -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please. The Prosecution has no objection on the assumption that somehow at some point the relevance of women fighting or not fighting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's not plain to me. And so now I'm hoping, I assume that later, the relevance of this will be made clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever lived a trial in which you knew exactly what to expect during the first week --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A trial here at this Tribunal. Because at home, yes, of course. The answer is definitely yes. But over here the answer is definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just make my reservations clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Judge Eser would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Before you go on with this list I have a question with regard to the English translation and whether it is concurrent with the Serbian original. In the English translation you read: "Of women who should be paid for the months of August." Now, should be paid does not necessarily imply that it has been paid. So was it only a list of requests for people to be paid or was it a document of salaries paid in fact? And what is the original? Does the translation correspond to the original?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there may be a slight difference in the translation. It says: "List of women who should be paid their salaries for the month of August." This means that they have done their job and that they are to be paid. It doesn't mean that they -- I ask that the interpreters confirm what I say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I may be of some help. Does it actually mean to be entitled to be paid? Is this what the document says? Having a right to be paid in other words?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the relevance of my question will be clear immediately from my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are you sure that your own unit had no women soldiers in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for a fact that it didn't. I didn't see any women.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO document 01320487, a list of conscripts of the Jezestica II Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 26, Mr. Simic, if you would take a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just move the document up a little bit so we can see number 26. 26, the name is Vida Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, in your testimony you mentioned a person who was killed, and this person's name was Vida?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same person?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see that it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Simic, Vida Trisic was a soldier, was she not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether she was a soldier or not, but in 1993, that's when she was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that document number 013220487, list of conscripts in the Jezestica II Company be admitted into evidence. And I also move that the previous document, number 00656840 bearing the list -- the title: "List of women to be paid salaries for August 1992" be admitted into evidence. I was interrupted, so that's why I did not enter it right away. I can repeat this for the registry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to Madam Vidovic. The first one -- yes, the first one with ERN number 00656840 and 00656841 will be D20. And the last document, 013204 -- I think it's 57 and not 87, if I can read it or 67 but not 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please just one matter. Was -- Madam Vidovic put to the witness that Vida --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Trisic was mentioned in this witness's testimony. I wonder if Madam Vidovic could be so kind as to remind the Prosecution when this happened -- Friday I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine so. I cannot -- I do recall him mentioning some people being killed, but not the names. I mean, I don't remember the names.
