utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Madam Vida --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Roberts will help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll give you the line number. It's page 59, Your Honours, that's when Madam Vida was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And this document will be D21.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you said that the Kravica and Jezestica areas, the entire local communes did not have an organised command and that there was no commander.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you mentioned a certain Nikolic from Kravica coming to Jezestica for negotiations, talks.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was after the fall on the 8th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Does the name Jovan Nikolic mean anything to you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him but I don't know why -- what the context was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can this person, Nikolic, be connected to Jovan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me intervene here. If I remember well -- I mean, I'm relying on my memory which usually isn't that bad. Last time, last Friday, you mentioned a certain Dragan Nikolic as being the person that visited your village or wherever after the fall of 8 August. Now it's being put to you -- another name is being put to you, Jovan Nikolic. Are these the name person? Could you have been wrong last time when you said Dragan Nikolic and you meant to be Jovan Nikolic or do you stay by what you told us last time, the name you mentioned last time, and identified Jovan Nikolic as someone different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It was Dragan Nikolic who came after the fall in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic -- Mr. Simic, I apologise, Mr. Simic, is it correct that during April, May, and June 1992 the surrounding Muslim villages were cleansed, or rather that the Muslim population was expelled from around your village?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not clear to me. I don't know -- I was at home. I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you are a sensitive man. Last Friday you became tearful remembering your house, and I assume you would feel for the fate of your neighbours, including Muslims. Can you tell us what happened to the Muslims from your neighbourhood. Did you know anything at all about this?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not told anything. If I had heard or seen anything, I would tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher put on the ELMO a map of Bratunac drawn up by the Republican Bureau of Statistics of the Republic of Croatia which is part of the document of the ethnic composition of Bosnia and Herzegovina by villages, and this was published in Zagreb in April 1995. And would the usher -- we have a map in colour. Please put it on the ELMO and let the witness look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness please take a good look at this map.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you focus --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, please. Yes, Judge Brydensholt -- it's okay. Please go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please focus on the map itself -- yes. Thank you. Thank you. Now it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, would you please take a look at these villages and is it correct that the green circles, I apologise both to the Chamber and to the witness, these darker circles appear to me to be green, they are green in the original. Mr. Simic, could you tell us whether the green circles really indicate the Muslim settlements while the violet ones indicate Serb settlements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, again it's even having the printout, photocopied printout itself, doesn't help much when talking about colours. But then seeing it on a monitor you are further disadvantaged. Do you have available this map or this chart and map and details in the original, in other words coloured? Because, I mean, it's easy for you to put the question: Look at those circles which are -- seem to be darker than the others, but this is a photocopy. I mean, it can be very misleading, very misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there's one other aspect about this map that's of concern to me. This witness is not a demographics man, he's plainly not an expert in demographics. I've got no problem, if Your Honours please, of Madam Vidovic exploring with this witness movements in the area. I've got no problem with that whatsoever, and I'm not trying to stop her. But trying to do it by presenting a map of demographics to this witness is, with respect, not the way to go about it. She can ask this witness: Did all the Muslims move out of certain villages? And he can tell you. He will probably be of assistance to you, more in that manner rather than commenting on a demographics map. If the Defence wishes to tender this map into evidence, I've got no objection to that and they can do that straight away. All I'm concerned about is getting the witness to comment on this particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the witness could perhaps be in a position to comment. I mean, he could be in a position. I mean, coming from the Mediterranean region where communities live closer than in many other places, I can assure you that I wouldn't be surprised in the least if the witness can come forward and tell us village by village whether they were predominantly Muslim or predominantly Serb, or predominantly -- I can tell you in my country each hamlet --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I've got no problem with that and Your Honour, I think, reflects what I just told the Trial Chamber. I've got no problem with that line of examination, but it's the use of the map and it's commenting on it that is -- it's a bit unfair with this witness who may have some trouble reading and understanding demographics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is granted. That I grant you. I have the same problems as well. I personally cannot really follow from here because it's -- the shading that you have on a photocopy like this may not reflect the different colours only. It may be the result of second, third, fourth, fifth, or 90th generation photocopy. So I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to simplify this. Let us forget about green and blue circles. I will just ask the witness the following question: Mr. Simic -- and I certainly would not request this map to be tendered as a Defence exhibit. I will only ask the witness the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show to the Trial Chamber Glogova and Hranca irrespective of the colour of the circles?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please do that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see Glogova first.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then Hranca, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether those were at the time, 1991, at the beginning of war populated by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glogova was a Muslim village, whereas Hranca was a mixed one, a mixture of both the Serbian and the Muslim populations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Simic. How far is Glogova from Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but I think it's about 6 kilometres between Jezestica and Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show to the Trial Chamber the village of Jecevo [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can. How about Voljavica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me also tell you that Bljeceva also had a mixed population.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What many Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. There were both Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it predominantly a Muslim village? Was that a predominantly Muslim or Serb village?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they were both nationalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, sir. Do you agree that Glogova was an exclusively Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as you -- which is as you say about 6 kilometres far away. Could it have been possible that in May you heard nothing about a mass murder of civilians that took place there, of Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Shots were heard, but I don't know where they came from, but I didn't hear about the specific event, that that was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, is it true that there were permanent fighting with the residents of the surrounding Muslim villages, include Jezestica, in the period between May and August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me, but I know that in Polje, where my house is, was not involved. As for the other hamlets, I never heard from anyone. They also just kept guard around their houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness the Defence exhibit number 002075886. It starts with the village of Hranca and it contains the list of casualties in Hranca and Glogova. And for now, I will only deal with the list of the dead and the wounded in Hranca -- I'm sorry, in Glogova. Could the witness please be shown page 02075887.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the list of the wounded in Glogova at various times. Mr. Simic, do you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- I don't know any of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, please pay attention to numbers 45 and 46 in the list, Ljubomir Rankovic [phoen] and Milica Rankovic [phoen] who were from Jezestica, therefore from your village. And it says that they were wounded in Glogova on the 2nd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I never heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Glogova is a Muslim village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I would also like to draw your attention that on that same day, the 2nd of August, 1992, in Glogova, according to this document, Vojo Avromovic [phoen] from Kravica was also wounded. Could you please look at this, Mr. Simic. This is your native town. Goran from Kravica, Dusko Milanovic [phoen] from Kravica. Number 31, Dusko Nikolic from Kravica; number 43, Drago Radovic from Bratunac. All of them were wounded on the 2nd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any of those people whose names you've just read.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, is it possible that those men on that day were involved in the fighting with the Muslims from Glogova, in other words that they were attacking Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can please this list of casualties in Glogova that I just quoted be tendered as Defence exhibit and that it be given a number. And this document is also -- it came from the confiscated documentation of the 5th Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska, the Sokolac collection about which Ms. Resina told us today that the 5th Corps is a legal successor of the Drina Corps that used to operate at the time in this zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for the information. Just for the record, that is not being taken as evidence on your part, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, does this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That document will be D22, by the way. It's up to her. If Madam Vidovic -- we now have that map or -- and accompanying information in colour. And basically you have the violet or the mauve and the green. If you want to make use of it and introduce it in evidence, we will concede you that without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would certainly wish that if there is no problem because my -- we have only one coloured copy and that was my main concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it can be photocopied in colour. We will do it for you. So -- yes, Mr. Di Fazio, you have problems with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no. None at all. Just a clerical issue, so to speak. I just wanted to be sure, D22, is that with ERN numbers ending 887 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 886. It starts with 886.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Then I've got a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then there is a corresponding page in English and it continues with 887 right through 888, and then there are two pages in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then 889, corresponding page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 892 and a corresponding page in English. That's what I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's what I have, too, but the whole bundle is being tendered. That's what I'm not sure about. Because it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't take it as if the whole bundle was being taken, and I take it that only this was being tendered today. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I thought that what was being tendered as a result of the cross-examination that was just conducted was a very specific part of this bundle. I thought it was 887 and 888 and the accompanying English translation. If I'm wrong, that's what I want to be clear about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's check what Madam Vidovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's how I was following the evidence, you see, Looking at the list and the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems to me that I was quite clear and that I referred to 02075887, the list of casualties from Glogova, should be tendered as Defence exhibit. Truly I did refer to the Prosecution number that has at the beginning of this document for -- to make it more convenient for the Prosecution because I'm using their bunch of documents and didn't want to tire the Chamber with the whole set of documents that referred to some other issue. So I was quite clear when I said I wanted the document to be tendered which ends in numbers 887.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically it's this set of numbers that are being tendered. And for convenience sake, we could actually take off 0207886 and take off the rest, but I would keep everything as it is, Mr. Di Fazio, I mean, starting from 02075886 to 02075889.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I've got no problem with either course. All I wanted to know is precisely what is being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I read what Madam Vidovic said. I never -- can, please, this list of casualties in Glogova that I just quoted be tendered as a defence exhibit, and that it be given a number. And this document is also -- it came from the confiscated documentation of the 5th Corps of the army of VRS, the Sokolac collection, and she continues. But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But the names mentioned and the accompanying -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I've got -- I followed Ms. Vidovic's evidence perfectly fine. I make no complaint about that at all. It's just that she, as I understood it, was looking at, referring to, and leading and taking this witness through 887 and 888. And that's what I thought was being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but she said first she will deal with Glogova and then she will deal with Hranca. So I suspect that she still has to deal with Hranca. I don't know. I mean, it's -- I don't know what to expect because I'm not in her mind. I don't know. Let's not complicate matters, Mr. Di Fazio. I mean, I'm quite happy with this -- these four or five pages being D22 and then we'll make of them what we need to at a later stage. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm really doing my best to finalise my cross-examination as soon as possible, but if we proceed along these lines I am not sure I can be blamed if that doesn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, let me go back to this document --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The map gets an exhibit number D23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be -- the map will be D23? Yes. I'm giving it back to you so that you make a photocopy of it then please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, doesn't this document that I just showed you indicate that something was going on and that there was fighting in the days that preceded the attack of the 8th August that you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document that shows that several persons had been wounded in Glogova, in your view does it confirm that there was fighting going on in Glogova in those days in early August that preceded the attack of the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honours. I will move on with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I will ask you about some facts relating to the attack itself. Can you tell me why were the Muslims unable to enter the valley of the village of Jezestica or Nova Jezestica, as it is called locally.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, inasmuch as they wanted to occupy the territory they did so and they could return.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the Serbian TO did not put up any resistance on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to the same extent as the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by not to that extent? To what extent did they put up resistance? Will you please slow down, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very few of us. As I said on Brdo were very few men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The few men that you referred to -- so did these few men put up any resistance? Did they open fire?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were very few Serbian forces of the village defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You said that you were standing on the hill and that Rankovici were on one side whereas on the other side you were able to have Djermani and Jezestica. Can you tell this Chamber the exact name of the site from which you were able to see on both sides?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's called Brdo, the hill. And that is the point for which I could see Kijevici, Djermani and Jezestica, the hamlets, and Rankovici. And after that we descended to another location from which we could see Rankovici better and the name of this location is Gajice.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said the name of this location is Gajice?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many Muslim soldiers precisely did you see on the day of the attack of the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact number because they were moving in one direction. First they set fire to one part and then they went on to Rankovici and set fire to the other part.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Simic, tell us approximately how many there were?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 40 or 50 men, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can tell but there may have been more.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. What did these men look like? How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them had camouflage uniforms, others had green uniforms and there were women and children there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these full camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were entire uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what were the women and children doing?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carrying food off and leading off cattle and livestock.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you were not able to see who was setting fire to the villages, could you? Were you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see them as soon as they left the houses. There would be smoke and then it would burst into flames. And as I said on Friday, it's all there as if on a plate. You can see it very easily because we were up on a hill and this is in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will remind you that on Friday you said the following: The soldiers started the fires and then the women and children went in and took things, and this went on for about an hour. Doesn't it seem strange to you, Mr. Simic, that first the houses should be set on fire and then women and children should go in into the burning houses to take things?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said on Friday, and I abide by that, the women and children took the livestock from the barns and they collected the food. There was nothing to be found inside the houses except for a little bread. That's what I said on Friday and that's what I'm saying today.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, let me remind you that in your statement of the 7th of April, 2001, on page 3, paragraph 2, Prosecution number 03062100, you said: "I saw the Muslims setting fire to our houses. We could not see the faces of those who were setting fire to the houses." You did not say at that time that these were soldiers. Why have you now changed your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Let's do this the proper way. If you are referring him to a statement that he made and it's also important that we follow, please let's get the statement and make it available to the witness. That's the first part. Secondly, again, the corresponding number, ERN number of course doesn't correspond to the English version, so we need to check that as well. This is the witness of -- the statement of the 7th of April. Can we have the statement of the witness of the 7th of April of 2001 shown to him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean the B/C/S version. It's no use showing him the English version. But we need to follow in the English version. And in the English version which paragraph are we referring to, because in the second paragraph was mentioned by Madam Vidovic on page 3, but that doesn't necessarily correspond to what we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was thinking of the Bosnian version. I do apologise. When preparing my cross-examination, in future I will always provide both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's not you who has to provide them, Madam Vidovic. I think they must be made available to the witness if he is being asked to comment on the parts of his statement, then he should have his statement available. But that's the registrar's --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He does have it available, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you -- do you have it before you, Mr. Simic, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And which paragraph from the end - from this we're talking of page 3 - which paragraph from the end in the Bosnian Serb version would that be, counting from the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the part that is highlighted. I'm asking the witness to look at the highlighted part that says: "At that moment I saw ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am referring to the -- I am just asking you to tell me in the Bosnian Serb language, which paragraph would this be starting from -- counting from the very last paragraph because we have the English version here, and we don't have it highlighted of course. Starting from the last --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the third paragraph from the bottom or the second from the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but the second from the top in your version. It changes in the English version. Yes, now can you read out to the witness the part you want him to comment upon, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in this part: "I saw Muslims setting fire to our houses. We were not able to see the faces of those who set fire to the houses."

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But they were soldiers and they were Muslims. They were not Serbs. And I did say "Muslims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see it in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see it in the English, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's page 3. The number 3 is partially obscured by the signature. It's about midway through the first paragraph. Do you see the words: "At that stage we saw the Muslims" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How does the paragraph start?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The first attack on the village of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not three paragraphs from the end, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the confusion. I mean, we can't go on like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I respectfully agree. If Your Honours please, the problem with this is that what the witness has before him is a translation of his statement. His statement was taken in English and read back to him. And that's the portion that should be put to him. Now, who knows if there were mistakes committed in the B/C/S translation later or not. But his statement that was read back to him and he signed is in English. Now, I don't see any problem with Madam Vidovic putting portions from the English statement to the witness and the interpreters can interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Me neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I raise one other matter. I don't know if Miss -- Madam Vidovic wants to try and develop this point, I'm not entirely sure where she is going, but the English statement is redolent with reference to Muslim forces. It's peppered throughout. Everywhere you look on this statement, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, please don't proceed with these comments in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours, but it's a rather obvious matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the problem is we have to find a more practical way of presenting -- because this is only the beginning. I mean, we are going to have an endless number of witnesses coming forward showing their statements, which I agree is usually tendered in English and then translated into B/C/S, and we need to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours. May I suggest that if prior statements of the witness are going to be put to him then they have to come from the English statement and be interpreted because that's his statement. That's what was read back to him on the 7th of April, 2001, by the interpreter, Marina Krstic [phoen] and she provided her certification. And his acknowledgment at the end of the statement also on that date is that he -- it's been read to him in Serbian and he then went ahead and signed it. That's -- it may be in English, but that's what he acknowledged. That's his statement, not the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, let's not waste more time on this. We'll regulate this as we go along. Yes, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already explained that I was working on the basis of the version in Bosnian. In future I will respect your wishes and I will always provide both versions. For the present, I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I will now ask you something else. You remember that on Friday you mentioned the village of Cumavicani. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said then that you heard from them that a certain Kemo had taken a severed head to Srebrenica with him.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a village called Cumavicani near Srebrenica. It was occupied on the 7th of January, 1993. I heard from -- if I have to, I will tell you the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did ask you who you heard it from.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Radinka Vujadinovic who had been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say, Mr. Simic, that she was in Cumavici at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. She was in Cumavici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not correct, Mr. Simic, that the exchange of the local Serbian population from the village of Cumavici was carried out in June 1992. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. But I did hear from her and she said to me: You can speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. I will now put some question to you relating to the attack on Kravica and Jezestica on the 7th of January, 1993. Is it not correct, Mr. Simic, that the VRS, including your units which you call defence or whatever, attempted to cleanse the Eastern Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Bosnia area known as Podrinje of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. It's possible, but I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not correct, Mr. Simic, that persistent attacks were mounted on the Muslim population in which the Bratunac Brigade participated with the intention of -- from the area of Bratunac, which includes the Kravica area, with the intention of expelling the entire Muslim population from that area?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that either. I didn't see that. I can't say that here. I don't know who did what.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are you aware that the Bratunac Brigade in your area carried out large combat activities with the clear aim of attacking the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not clear to me either. From my house I never went far. On Christmas -- on the 7th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. This is not the proper answer to the question that was put to you. Mr. Simic, the question that was put to you was the following, it did not refer to the 7th of January of 1993 or to any particular date for that matter. It said: "Are you aware that the Bratunac Brigade in your area carried out large combat activities with the clear aim of attacking the Muslim population?" So the question was -- refer to any time, not just the 7th of January. You may sit down. Sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible, but I neither heard nor saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would the usher please put on the ELMO document starting with 00641755 entitled: "The war history of Bratunac. The circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the outbreak of the war." Pages 00641766 and page -- for now we'll stick to this page. Will the usher please show Mr. Simic page number 00641766, and I am going to quote the third paragraph which reads, and I kindly ask the witness to look at it and comment on it: "On the 25th of December, 1992" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record in the English version we are referring to 00840182, and that's the last paragraph on page 13, what is shown as page 13. And that's precisely two, four, six, eight, nine lines before the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to quote. "On the 25th of December, 1992, the command of the Bratunac Brigade issued an order to recapture the temporarily occupied territories by the Muslim units as follows: The battalion number 1 was ordered to take up positions in the area of Hranca village/S. Drina TT17. The second battalion with the platoon (Zenica) to take up control of the road down the Drina river and down the Bratunac/Opati/Banovici [phoen] road. The third battalion to organise circular defence in the area of Kravica. The Krajski [phoen] Battalion shall take up the Repovac road TT422. Second section on the right from the first battalion and the Bratunac/Kravica road. During the day upon orders of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and KDK, the brigade command received the visit from the military police from the protective regiment headed by Major Cavcic Milomir [phoen] whose task was to control the movement of military conscripts in the town and to bring in deserters to secure the Ljubovija most on the -- the Ljubovija bridge on the river Drina --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we don't have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise for that. If we are proceeding with this document any further, will -- first of all, the witness -- let's have the witness answer the question first, but you put the question basically. Yeah, could you put the question, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, have you seen this document -- can you see that an order was issued to capture the temporarily occupied territories including the village of Hranca?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you then a different question regarding this document. Can the village of Hranca be considered by the Muslims as a temporarily occupied territory? Were any Muslims living in Hranca prior to this time?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Because I travelled there before the attacks and I never went anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Simic, you just told us that Hranca was, to say the least, a mixed Muslim and Serbian village in the map. It was marked with green colour which indicates predominantly Muslim village. Were you aware that there were Muslims living in Hranca before January 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were also -- there were both the Muslims and the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So including the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There's another question that I would like to ask you concerning this document, Mr. Simic. Here there's the mention of battalions, the people from Zenica. Doesn't it seem to me that, Mr. Simic, you should have known about such a massive concentration of troops in the area where you were living?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible, but it was not in the vicinity of Jezestica where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please pages 00641766 -- in fact, only this page for the moment, and the first page which indicates what document we are talking about be tendered as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what about the rest? 00641767.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the moment I ask Your Honours to allow this part to be tendered as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's going to split. Again, Madam Vidovic, you are conducting the case as if it is being conducted in your own language. The English translation does not correspond to the same pagination that you have. In fact, if you look at the British -- the English translation, we don't even have cross-reference to the B/C/S version. And the B/C/S version that we have, page 00641766 seems or purports to be a continuation of a previous page, which according to the papers that we were given is not 765 but it's 755. So we need to know where we are. We are going to break now. Deal with this -- we will admit of course whatever you would like to have admitted in evidence from this document, but we do not because we have to admit it in B/C/S and also in English. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The difficulty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't see any problem to have the whole document beginning with 00641755, including its pages 00641766 and 767 be tendered as Defence exhibits. And we are going to try and stick to this procedure in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That makes it better. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, did you want to remark?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there's all the matters that you raised. I have nothing further to add, of course, to what Your Honours have raised. But, is this a document? Is this a book? Where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it it is part of the same document we had before. If I recognise it. Let me just check. Yes. It is exactly the -- from the same document D15. In fact, the first page has the same ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But of course the pages that follow now are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a short break of 25 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we received this from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and we'll resume soon after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, Madam Vidovic, Mr. Simic, again my recommendation to go slow not to disrupt the day of the interpreters and the reporter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me just check whether the last exhibit was given number D24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Now, I would like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO document number 0675533. That's the report by the Bratunac Brigade, strictly confidential, number 119, dated the 4th of January, 1994, addressed to the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Because you said "1994." I think you should have said "1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 1993. I wasn't aware of having said "1994." So the 4th of January, 1993. Could the witness please look at the quote under number 2, and it reads in the report that: "Our forces are conducting operations along the Valjevo, Vinjista, Kravica, and the Veljko, Glogova, Vradusic [phoen], Petkovici, i Brezaksanici [phoen] - sonic [phoen] TT403, Vinjista axis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this part of the document, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you know that the surrounding Muslim population was attacked on the 4th of January, 1993 by the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear of any attack taking place on that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, please look at the last sentence of item 2 of this document which reads: "The operation continued on the 4th of January, 1993, until full capturing of the Bratunac/Kravica road." Therefore, Mr. Simic, this was an extensive operation. How was it possible that you knew nothing about this?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I heard shooting, but I don't know who did what and I think that was an exchange of fire. But I was not involved in that and I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can document number 00675533, the Bratunac Brigade's report, strictly confidential, number 119, dated the 4th of January, 1993, addressed to the command of the Drina Corps be admitted as the Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is so admitted and it will be marked exhibit D25.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask now the usher to put on the ELMO document number 01321055 and immediately thereafter document number 01321054. The document number 01321055 is entitled: "The list of the wounded on the 5th of January, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Simic, can you look at this list. Isn't it true that this document demonstrates that seven Serbian soldiers were wounded on the 5th of January, 1993? Isn't it also true that behind each of these names there's an indication of the unit that they belonged to? Can you please look at number 1 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's mention the name please because we have got two pages here --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is Nedeljko, father's name Djuric, Nenad, born in 1966, Krajina battalion. So the point of my question was: Does it read here the Krajina battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't heard of that, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I will draw your attention to the following document entitled: "The list of the wounded on the 6th of January," and that it shows the names of Cvijana Obackic and Mladjena Jovanovic. Both were wounded in Glogova. Is that correct, Mr. Simic? You don't -- these names don't mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not familiar with these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please I object to the manner in which this document is being used. The witness says he doesn't know about this document. I don't mind Madam Vidovic showing him the document and then asking him about the contents of the document. Do you know Stojan? Do you know Petrovic? Was he in the 1st Battalion. Was he wounded, in fact. I don't mind that sort of thing, but it's not being approached in that fashion. And it should be in the Prosecution's submission. He doesn't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the other hand, Mr. Di Fazio, if we were to change place you will do exactly what I am doing, intervening the least possible, because otherwise it will become a never-ending story.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The only reason -- I realise, if Your Honours please, it's causing no harm to the Prosecution because all we have to do is come back and say to Your Honours that our latter -- pointing -- you knew nothing about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will take more time if we direct counsel to put questions differently. The fact is that I think the witness himself is understanding what is being required from him because he is giving the answer: I know or I don't know these persons. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm going to ask the witness something about this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, were you aware that these units, the 4th Zenica Battalion and the people from Loznica, which is in Serbia, were involved in the fighting in the area of Glogova which was your neighbourhood and that was on the 6th of January on the eve of the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about that nor had I heard of it. I cannot confirm anything here that I know nothing about and I heard nothing about. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, on the 6th of January and the 5th of January, that is before the 7th of January attack, did you hear any shooting taking place in the villages around you, Jezestica and Kravica I mean?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that there was shooting coming from all sides, from the Muslim side and from the Serbian side. But what you are implying here I never heard of these men nor do I know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Simic. Thank you. I kindly ask the Chamber that these documents pages 01321055 and 01321054 be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. They are being admitted as marked. I take it if I don't hear an objection from your part, we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They are being -- these pages are being tendered and marked as document D26.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, in your testimony on Friday you said and mentioned that people were killed during the attack on Jezestica and Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask the usher to put on the ELMO document number RR322082. Can the witness please look at this list which says: "The list of the killed fighters from the Kravica area." So the list of the fighters who were killed from the area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there are 34 fighters here including men from Jezestica? Can you please look carefully at this document. There are columns: Name and the place of residence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can the usher please, yes, move it a little bit upwards so we can see the full list. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my statement I said that I don't know, but I heard about the people from Kravica. I know that people were collected from Jezestica, and that is what I said in my statement. I did hear, though, that about 30, 32, or 34 of them were killed on the 7th of January, 1993, in the vicinity of Kravica. And as I said in my statement, those men were gathered there, but I never saw them. I know that they were in Jezestica and that in the hamlet of Jezestica five brothers were killed and there was also some family members killed and that made up this number of 35 or 36. And that was in the period since -- between the 8th of August, 1992, until the 7th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Mr. Simic, were the fighters from Jezestica also mentioned in this list?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are fighters but there are also civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can you please look very carefully at this list and tell us who among these people is a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Kravica I said I don't know these people and how many of them were killed and who of them were civilians or fighters. I can tell you about --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among this list which says: "The list of fighters," can you tell me who among these people were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all from Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look, Mr. Simic, at the column in the middle. There are many names originally from Jezestica. I am just reading what it says here in this document. So there are plenty of names of people from Jezestica. Please look at their age. Mr. Simic, can you please answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that there were four civilians from Jezestica. The rest were all fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you point out these names.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Risto Ostojic was a fighter. Ostojic, Mitar, was a fighter, Radovan Pavlovic, I don't know about him; Kostadin Pavlovic, I also don't know about him; Vojo Radovic; Gojko Radovic, I don't know about those either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is unnecessarily confusing and compounding the matter in an unbelievable manner. The question was very simple. Amongst the persons on this list which in column 4 supposedly came from Jezestica, do you see any names that you can confirm to us as being civilians and not fighters. At a certain moment I heard you say or at least the interpretation that reached us was: Yes there are four. Could I have the names of those four, and then if necessary check the rest. But could you give us the names of those four first. Which are the four gentlemen from Jezestica that were not fighters but according to you were civilians who were killed on the 7th of January, 1993, in the Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just take a look at this list. Last name Djukanovic, that was a female. Krsto Djukanovic, we used to call him Kidjo, he was freed. That's what I heard about him. And there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he freed or was he killed? Because this is supposedly what I have here, if it has been translated properly, is a list of persons, fighters, who were killed in the Kravica area on the 7th of January of 1993. And who is the female, because under Bukanovic, Ivan, and I see Hrsto [phoen]. Hrsto. None of them are a woman. At least if I -- I don't know your language, but I can understand enough of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are no women's names here, at least I did not see any and I have studied the list carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are going to make me turn into a dentist, Mr. Simic. I will do it the only way that will get me there. Number 3 Bogicevic, Radojko, do you know if he was a civilian or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 10, Jovanovic, Radomir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 11, Miladinovic, Ratko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was also a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Radinovic, Djordjo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Milanovic, Nedjo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Milanovic, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ostojic, Milan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ostojic, Mitar, number 19.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was exempt but he was killed on the 7th of January. He was at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So number 32, Bukanovic, Bosko --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bosko Djukanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Bosko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was exempt but he was also killed. He was killed at his home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Djukanovic, Ivan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a fighter and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Djukanovic, Krsto.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was exempt and he was killed at his home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Does that answer your question, Madam Vidovic? Let's proceed to the next question. One moment, I apologise to Judge Eser. Judge Eser has been drawing my attention, had a question. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: My question is related to this list. You have been speaking of fighter, at least in the English translation. Or do you mean this fighter, does it mean to be a soldier, and if so, a soldier of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the Bratunac Brigade and it is a list of killed fighters referring to soldiers from the Kravica area. When the witness says "exempt" I assume he means exempt from military service. However, this document does not mention any such. It simply says that there are lists of fighters killed in the Kravica area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But the translation of the word --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] It's killed fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fighters. It's fighters and not soldiers. That's the combatants, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I rather thought that the witness might answer Judge Eser's question rather than Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, but the question was more related to basically whether the use of the word "fighter" on the document on the English version is the correct translation of the corresponding word in B/C/S or whether it should be "soldier." And it is obvious that we've got the answer. It's not "soldier" but "fighter." I take it as combatant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Have you finished with this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I move that the document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's being tendered and accepted as document D27.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question in connection with this for Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, does the fact that many people were killed at that time indicate that there was fierce fighting in Jezestica between the Serb and Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a large-scale attack by the Muslim forces. There was firing on all sides. We saw that there was nothing we could do and began to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was whether your fighters participated in the combat, the ones who were killed. Did they mount any resistance? Did they shoot?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends. Some were withdrawing and were killed while withdrawing, while retreating; they were by the road, at least that's what I heard. I didn't go to see for myself. I stayed at my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment Madam Vidovic. I think at this point, Mr. Wubben, I would suggest that you send your next witness home. At the same time, Madam Vidovic, I'm making it clear that you need to finish, conclude, your cross-examination before the end of the day. We will not proceed with this witness tomorrow, in other words. Thank you. And please do convey the apologies of the Chamber to your witness and I will then apologise to her in public tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We will do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO the photograph of Mr. Simic's house. Prosecution Exhibit Number -- it was exhibited on Friday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record we are looking at 01087849. Correct me if I'm wrong. This is the photo with the writing on it, no? Could we have it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, very briefly, please give me a very brief reply, you can see certain letters, four Cyrillic letters, S. Do you think this is short for "only unity will save the Serbs"?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. When I got back I saw this there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. In connection with this I will put a question to you. Isn't it correct, Mr. Simic, that after the fighting you testified about on the 7th of January, 1993, in Kravica, there followed large-scale combat activities in the Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is possible but I didn't see it. I was fleeing. While I was fleeing I saw there were forces there but I didn't see anything else. We had wounded there. We were taking them away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will put the question a little differently. Is it correct, Mr. Simic, that the Serb forces took large-scale offensive action in the area of Jezestica, Kravica, and other villages during January, February, and March 1993? You should know that.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this. What forces? Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb forces. Again, I can tell you that every day you heard shooting on all sides. Nobody knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I am asking you. So there were battles?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were battles on both sides. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now put on the ELMO a document issued by the command of the Bratunac Brigade, strictly confidential, number 290 through 93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there going to be a re-examination on your part, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I know what Your Honours -- want this witness to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, of course, and I have to regulate the time accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've got a number of issues that I think I can get down to 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much minutes, I'm talking of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Five to eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That doesn't leave us with anything else. We are going to put our foot down. You have played literally into this, perhaps without wanting it, but you have literally tied our hands. We will be imposing time limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to finish in not more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Would the usher put on the ELMO Bratunac Brigade document 290/93 dated the 11th of February, 1993, 01331793.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, would you please look at this document, item 2 of the daily combat report reads as follows: "Our forces, the focus of activities in the Banovici/Kravica area where the battalion attacked. This 3rd Infantry Battalion, sir, this is the one where your name is listed as having received a salary in November. It also says: "The enemy strongly resisted in this direction." Have you seen this document now?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, I will ask you: Is it possible that the destruction of the Kravica area including Jezestica, bearing in mind the graffiti on your house occurred after the 7th of January, 1992, during this fierce fighting?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the graffiti was put on my house. I know it wasn't there when I left it on the 7th of January, but it was there when I came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But will you please answer just the following question: Is it not correct that you returned to your house together with the Serbian army after it had again retaken Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned, as I said in my statement, until I heard from Miladin Bogdanovic that there was a commission. And then I came to the military department in Bratunac but I went to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. Did the Serbian army fight to retake Kravica during the second half of January, February, and March 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions. This document of the Bratunac Brigade may be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted as document D28. Thank you. You have not more than five minutes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very limited. Let's just try and be a little precise about some things at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, a question just put do you a matter of seconds ago by Madam Vidovic: Is it not correct that you returned to your house together with the Serbian army after it had retaken Kravica. You said you returned and then went on. Did you or did not return with the Serbian army or did you return by yourself, that is not as part of the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not part of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown D27.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all let me ask you while the document is being presented to you: A gentleman named Nedjo Milanovic, you know him, from the Jezestica rea apparently. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedjo Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number 13 on the list. Look at number 13 on the list. Cast your eye down, go straight down. Number 13, Nedjo Milanovic, do you see him? Very quickly, do you see him there?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, he was born in 1937. That makes him about 67 years of age in 1992. Was he much of a fighter, as far as you can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think my learned friend misstated the age. The math is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. It makes a difference

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In -- go down to number 19 Mitar Ostojic, was he a young man in 1992? He was born in 1934. However old he was in 1992, was he a relatively young man or not?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. That Mitar Ostojic, he was exempt from the village guard, at least that's what I heard because he was ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. What about Krsto Bukanovic, number 34, how old was he? Was he an old man in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also exempt due to illness. He was at home and he was killed on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This purports to be a list of fighters from the Kravica area. Tell the Trial Chamber if you ever saw Krsto Bukanovic clamouring up hills with a gun, did you ever see such a sight? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bukanovic had his own rifle and he was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yeah, but my question is this: Did you ever see him in 1992 going out on patrol carrying guns, shooting at people, anything that might indicate in any sense at all, in any sense of the word, that he was a fighter?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see him do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. The Prosecutor is asking about 1992. This list is from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't really make a difference. We're talking about the same -- I'm surprised you asked him about Krsto and not about Bosko who was born in 1928.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I missed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. But, again, it's a question of having the eagle eyes or not, Mr. Di Fazio. Judge Brydensholt would like to put a question to you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes. Before you left your home on the 7th of January, 1993, was there any change made in order to make it easier defensible, any kind of fortification? Did you change anything regarding the doors or the windows or anything?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honour, the house was set on fire and it was gutted. There are still some remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I don't know whether it's a question of interpretation or not, but you didn't answer the question. The question that Judge -- do you allow me, Judge Brydensholt, to repeat your question or would you like to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was a simple one. On the 7th of January before you left, before you abandoned your home, your house, did you in any way try to protect it in any way by building barricades or by closing and barricading windows or doors? Did you try to protect it in any way or did you just close it and leave it?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left I closed the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do anything else. I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: But have you in the time before done any changes in order to make it easier to defend -- to use this as some sort of defence? Barricade the doors or barricade the windows before the attack? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I would like to come back to the time before the first attack when you established the village guard. What had been the reasons for establishing such a guard?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reasons were, Your Honour, that everybody had to protect his own house, otherwise they would set it alight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Against whom? There must have been a reason why you thought it necessary to protect yourself and your houses.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was so that the village would not be burned down. You had to stay by your house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But why had it been a threat that your village may be burnt down? Had there been some sort of controversy, animosity, with certain people in your area?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, between the Serbs and the Muslims because I was working in Belgrade and when I got back they said - that was on the 12th of March - they said you have to stay here because the village guard is being organised, so I had to stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But if I remember correctly you told us that you did not know of any events going on in Glogova, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, nobody told me anything. I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Judge Brydensholt. Thank you, Judge Eser. Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio and Madam Vidovic. Mr. Simic, this brings us to the end of your testimony. You're free to go now back to where you came from or where you would like to return. On behalf of the Tribunal and also on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser and also on my own behalf I should like to thank you for coming over to give evidence in this trial. You will be escorted out of the courtroom by the usher and you will be attended to by the rest of the staff of the Tribunal to make things easy for you to return home. Should you encounter any problems, please do let us know. Once more, thank you and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Assuming that there is no further business to deal with, I bring this session to an end. We have overstepped our time limit by about six minutes. Once more I thank the staff, the interpreters, the technicians, the reporter, everyone present anyway for having being indulgent with us for having stayed with us, operated, to have these extra five or six minutes. Tomorrow we'll start with the new witness. She hasn't got any protective measures in place, if I remember well, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll start at 9.00 in the morning. Thank you. And I understand it, you have withdrawn all documents that you meant originally to use with that witness, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday the 21st day of October, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
